summary: GeoNOVA is an AI-powered Earth-system intelligence and scientific investigation platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge, “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!” It integrates satellite imagery, historical environmental data, climate datasets, statistical analysis, and AI-assisted interpretation to help users understand how Earth's systems are changing over time. Built using Next.js, TypeScript, React, MapLibre GL, Python, and FastAPI, it features an interactive Earth map and rotating globe, Mission Control, Earth Trends Intelligence, Atmospheric Intelligence, Tectonic Intelligence, and a dedicated Science Workspace. It uses data and resources from NASA Earthdata, MODIS, OMI/Aura, AIRS, GPM, NASA POWER, USGS, Smithsonian, and ISRO/MOSDAC. Its capabilities include historical data retrieval, time-series generation, climate trend detection, statistical significance testing, seasonality analysis, spatial trend mapping, and multi-region comparisons. Through interactive maps, charts, research reports, and AI-assisted insights, GeoNOVA aims to transform complex Earth-observation data into understandable scientific evidence, helping users investigate what is changing, where it is changing, and how Earth's environmental systems are evolving.

GeoNOVA – AI-Powered Earth Observation & Scientific Trend Intelligence Platform

GeoNOVA is an AI-powered Earth observation and scientific intelligence platform designed to help researchers, students, and decision-makers investigate environmental changes and understand long-term trends across Earth's interconnected systems. Developed in response to NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026's “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!” challenge, GeoNOVA transforms complex Earth observation data into meaningful scientific insights through an integrated research and visualization environment.

What it does and how it works:
GeoNOVA brings together Earth science datasets from sources such as NASA Earthdata, NASA POWER, NASA EONET, USGS, Smithsonian, and ISRO-related services. Users can explore geographical regions through interactive maps and a globe-based Mission Control interface, investigate environmental variables, examine historical time series, and generate multi-region research reports. Its analytical engines support trend detection, linear regression, Mann–Kendall testing, Sen's slope estimation, statistical significance assessment, seasonal analysis, temporal dependence diagnostics, spatial trend analysis, and environmental anomaly investigation. AI-assisted research and evidence-analysis modules help organize findings and interpret scientific observations.

Benefits and intended impact:
GeoNOVA aims to make Earth system science more accessible, understandable, and evidence-driven. It can help users identify changing environmental patterns, investigate regional differences, examine possible anomalies, and communicate findings through visualizations and structured reports. By combining multiple scientific data sources with statistical methods, the platform encourages more transparent and reproducible environmental research. Its intended impact is to support climate awareness, environmental monitoring, scientific education, and informed decision-making.

Tools and technologies used:
The platform was developed using Next.js, React, TypeScript, and CSS for its frontend, with Python and FastAPI for backend processing. MapLibre GL powers interactive geospatial visualization. Scientific analysis is implemented through custom Python modules for time-series processing, statistical testing, seasonality, temporal dependence, spatial trends, and evidence validation. The project also integrates publicly available Earth observation and environmental data services.

Creativity and innovation:
GeoNOVA goes beyond displaying satellite data or individual environmental indicators. It combines interactive Earth visualization, multi-source scientific evidence, statistical trend detection, uncertainty and confidence analysis, AI-assisted interpretation, and automated research reporting within one platform. Its Mission Control interface and integrated Science Workspace provide a unified environment for exploring, analyzing, and communicating Earth system trends.

Factors considered during development:
The project considers scientific reliability, source transparency, data availability, geographical coverage, historical continuity, statistical significance, seasonality, temporal dependence, spatial variation, usability, and accessibility. It also distinguishes between observed patterns and statistically supported trends, helping users interpret results responsibly rather than treating every change as a confirmed scientific conclusion.

GeoNOVA's long-term vision is to become a comprehensive and accessible scientific intelligence platform that helps people better understand how Earth's systems are changing through data, analysis, and evidence-based insights.
